findings.statement: CPXM1 is raised in UC with a pooled log2FC of [gene=CPXM1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.8968], significant in seven of eight cohorts. It is also raised in non-inflamed mucosa of MSCCR (log2FC [gene=CPXM1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.0059]), so part of the change tracks the disease itself, not only local inflammation; heterogeneity between cohorts is high.

PCDH17 is a local marker of inflamed mucosa: in MSCCR it rises in inflamed biopsies (log2FC [gene=PCDH17; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.4831]) but only slightly in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=PCDH17; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.2776]). Caveat: only a small part of the bulk change is retained after composition adjustment, so much of the rise may reflect changed tissue composition.

LAIR2 is a T/NK-cell inflammation signal: it rises in inflamed MSCCR mucosa (log2FC [gene=LAIR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.3277]) and not in non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=LAIR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.1773], not significant). Caveat: a bulk increase in an immune gene may come from infiltrating lymphocytes; the cell-context specialist should confirm.

LILRA1 rises in inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=LILRA1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.3307]) with a small change in non-inflamed ([gene=LILRA1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.3679]). The signal is largely neutrophil/myeloid: per neutrophil the inflamed-vs-uninflamed change is small, so the bulk rise is mostly influx of cells, not a change inside the tissue. Weak as a target.

SERPINB5 is strongly and consistently up (all eight cohorts), with a paired inflamed-vs-non-inflamed log2FC of [gene=SERPINB5; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.0451] and a smaller rise in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=SERPINB5; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.0448]), so it is local to inflammation with a disease-level component. The change is intrinsic to epithelium (most of it kept after composition adjustment). Protein also rises in independent proteomics (log2 ratio [gene=SERPINB5; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.322]), though the authors did not call it significant.

CHI3L1 is among the largest and most reproducible increases (inflamed MSCCR log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=3.8187], up in all eight cohorts), and the protein also rises (log2 ratio [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607]). It is best read as a marker first.

CFB is raised across cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CFB; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.24], seven of eight cohorts significant), of epithelial origin and retained after composition adjustment, with a modest non-inflamed rise ([gene=CFB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.4765]) and a protein rise ([gene=CFB; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.238]).

SELP is a local-inflammation marker: inflamed MSCCR log2FC [gene=SELP; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.8372] versus non-inflamed [gene=SELP; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.4546].

RORC is modestly lower in inflamed MSCCR mucosa (log2FC [gene=RORC; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.4177]), but the paired inflamed-vs-non-inflamed change is nil ([gene=RORC; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-0.0627], not significant), so the loss reflects disease rather than local inflammation. The small size makes it a weak expression-supported target.

TUFM does not support the genetic hypothesis that inhibition helps: in inflamed MSCCR biopsies it is slightly lower, not higher (log2FC [gene=TUFM; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.188]), with no change in non-inflamed mucosa ([gene=TUFM; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.0115]). Weak candidate on expression grounds.

CEBPB is up in inflamed MSCCR mucosa (log2FC [gene=CEBPB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.7059]) and more strongly in UNIFI ([gene=CEBPB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE206285; layer=rna; cohort=GSE206285; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=2.046]; array and RNA-seq sizes are not comparable). It may partly reflect immune-cell infiltration (interpretation).

caveats: Only a subset of the pool genes was inspected in depth (CPXM1, PCDH17, LAIR2, LILRA1, SERPINB5, CHI3L1, CFB, SELP, RORC, TUFM, CEBPB); the others were only read from the pool dossier.
Microarray fold changes are compressed relative to RNA-seq; compare directions and significance across cohorts, not sizes.
Protein-level data were quantified only for a few genes; absence is not evidence against a gene.
Immune genes (LAIR2, LILRA1) may reflect neutrophil and lymphocyte infiltration; the cell-context specialist must confirm.
CFB safety (very high expression in vital organs, deficiency disease from gene loss) and CHI3L1 mixed mouse-colitis results come from the pool dossier and are for the safety/literature specialists.
